sentences.text: Sierraceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period found in New Mexico. It was a medium-sized horned dinosaur.
Its skull frill was relatively long with large holes separated by an oval-shaped midline bar.
Fossils were discovered in 1997 by geologist Gregory H. Mack on the Armendaris ranch in Sierra County, New Mexico.
The species was formally named and described in 2021 by Dalman, Lucas, Jasinski, and Longrich, with the publication appearing in 2022.
The animal is classified within the family Ceratopsidae and belongs to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
The dinosaur was originally classified under the genus Torosaurus before being reclassified.
Phylogenetic analysis places Sierraceratops as a sister species to Bravoceratops and Coahuilaceratops, forming a group endemic to the southwestern United States and Mexico.
Sierraceratops lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian epochs.
It is debated whether Sierraceratops and Torosaurus are the same animal, but closer study reveals distinct differences in their skull bars.
